title: AstraGrid Pilot Scope and Compliance Roadmap
summary: Initial POC scoping for a 6-week pilot. Main goals: validate latency and cost under AstraGrid workload, confirm SOC 2/ISO prerequisites, test SSO/SAML integration and RBAC matrix, and exercise audit logging/export. Agreed to run two benchmark passes (baseline + quantized) and provide security doc package by next Wednesday.
topics: Security/compliance: SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO attestations and security whitepaper (Maya) by 2025-07-23
Customer to share sample production prompts and 24h traffic profile (Evan) by 2025-07-18
Schedule first benchmark run (Diego + AstraGrid infra) week of 2025-07-28
action_items: Maya: Compile security package (SOC2 report, iso summary, RBAC docs) - due 2025-07-23
Evan: Provide sample prompt set and peak concurrency numbers - due 2025-07-18
Diego: Prepare benchmark harness and docker images for AstraGrid to run - due 2025-07-25
Lara: Share internal compliance checklist & known restrictions (data residency) - due 2025-07-20
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO, AstraGrid), Evan Kim (Platform Engineer), Lara Mendoza (Security Lead)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Rao: Priya here.
[00:08] Evan Kim: Evan.
[00:09] Lara Mendoza: Lara.
[00:11] Maya Chen: Awesome. Diego and I will walk through how we propose to scope the pilot and what security artifacts you'll need to sign off on the pilot, any immediate questions before we jump in?
[00:18] Priya Rao: No, let's dive. We're mainly focused on latency targets and data controls.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: Cool. high-level POC plan — six weeks, two benchmark passes: baseline with standard fp16-ish model and then a quantized pass to show cost drop while keeping quality. we want to simulate your live traffic — so we'll need sample prompts, sequence lengths, and concurrency.
[00:36] Evan Kim: Quick Q on quantized pass — will that be one of Redwood's off-shelf quant configs or something we control?
[00:42] Diego Alvarez: We bring recommended quant profiles, but it's configurable. For the pilot we usually run the vendor-recommended profile then a tuned run with customer-specific sequences. sometimes we see 20-40% token cost reduction with int8-like paths, but of course depends.
[00:56] Lara Mendoza: From security standpoint, the checklist is SOC 2 proximity plus ISO 27001 high-level attestation, SSO via SAML (we use Okta), RBAC mapping to our AD groups, and immutable audit logs. can you confirm Redwood supports per-request tenant tagging for logs?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Yes — we tag requests with customer_id and route_id fields. note: in older notes it might show as cust-id in some exports, but it's there. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM over s3 or syslog.
[01:26] Priya Rao: We need to ensure logs don't contain raw PII — do you support redaction/pseudonymization before export?
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: We have an optional redact step in the pipeline — it's rule-based and you can supply patterns. Important to test on your prompt corpus since transcription/predictions may leak entities. we also support on-prem/private deployment where logs stay inside your VPC.
[01:49] Evan Kim: For the pilot, we prefer Redwood Dedicated in VPC mode so traffic never leaves our network — is that feasible for a six-week pilot?
[01:57] Maya Chen: Yes, we can spin a Dedicated pool in your VPC for the pilot. There are two modes: temporary dedicated nodes for the POC or Private with customer-managed control plane; the former is faster to stand up. Diego, any infra lead times?
[02:08] Diego Alvarez: Typically 7-10 business days for Dedicated in VPC with our standard onboarding checklist — longer if there's custom firewall/NAT changes. We'll send the network requirements doc.
[02:19] Priya Rao: Sounds ok. On compliance docs, we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary, plus a data processing addendum. do you have those on file?
[02:29] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary. We'll share redacted SOC 2 and the ISO attestation. also the DPA template and KMS integration guide for BYOK.
[02:38] Lara Mendoza: BYOK is important. we use AWS KMS with custom key policies. can Redwood support key wrapping with our keys?
[02:46] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest; key wrapping and HSM-backed flows are supported in Private deployment mode. for Hosted there are limited BYOK options.
[02:57] Evan Kim: What about SSO — we use Okta SAML. expected auth integration time?
[03:02] Maya Chen: SAML SSO can be set up within a day for the console and API token scoping; integrating with RBAC to map roles to AD groups usually takes 2-3 days to configure and test.
[03:12] Priya Rao: On RBAC matrix — we need admin, dev, auditor roles and an automated way to rotate keys for auditor access. can the platform show audit entries for role escalations?
[03:21] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we log all role changes, API key rotations, and user assignments. the console surfaces these and we can push raw logs to your SIEM. there may be transcribed field names that differ (we've seen 'role_change' vs 'role-mod' in older exports), we'll confirm exact event names in the security package.
[03:36] Lara Mendoza: Great. on data residency — we need all inference logs to remain in eu-west-1. can you bind the pilot to that region?
[03:43] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we can pin the pilot to eu-west-1. There may be latency tradeoffs if your user base is mostly NA, but for compliance you'll get regional guarantees.
[03:52] Evan Kim: For benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood produce by default? p99 latency, p50, throughput?
[03:58] Diego Alvarez: We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail-latency distribution, tokens/sec throughput, tokens per dollar, and model perplexity/response quality metrics (via automated evals) when you provide references. We'll run a baseline pass and a quantized pass.
[04:12] Priya Rao: We'll want to define success criteria: p95 inference latency under 250ms for typical prompts, token cost under $0.0009/token for 2k average sequence. also fidelity threshold: ROUGE-like or human baseline score > 90% for our internal eval prompts.
[04:27] Diego Alvarez: Those are reasonable targets. We'll validate if the model family you choose can meet them under your concurrency. what peak qps do you expect?
[04:33] Evan Kim: Peak is about ~120 concurrent requests, average 40 rps sustained, typical prompt lengths: mean 600 tokens, tail to 2k.
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: For 120 concurrency with 2k tail lengths we should size the Dedicated pool accordingly. i'll propose an initial config: 8x A100-equivalent slots (or GPUs) with autoscale headroom. exact numbers after we run a smoke test.
[04:57] Priya Rao: We also need to test failure modes — say model fallback to smaller model when capacity saturated. do you support automatic fallback policies?
[05:04] Maya Chen: Yes — smart routing can fallback to compatible variants based on policy (latency-first or cost-first). We'll include a canary/fallback run in the pilot.
[05:11] Lara Mendoza: On the audit side, retention policy — can we set logs to 7 years? regulatory requires 7 in our vertical.
[05:18] Diego Alvarez: Long-term retention is an add-on; we can export to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules that match seven years. Need to confirm egress and storage costs in the pilot estimate.
[05:30] Evan Kim: For the first benchmark we'll want reproducible harness — can you provide docker images or terraform to spin up the runner?
[05:36] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll give a benchmark harness repo. it includes a dockerized runner, load generator config, and a step-by-step to reproduce. we'll also share a sample metrics dashboard.
[05:46] Priya Rao: How do we measure quality drift between baseline and quantized runs? automated evals are fine but we want human spot checks.
[05:53] Maya Chen: We'll run automated evals on a holdout set you provide and recommend a human review for a sample of 200 responses. we can also include a custom eval script if you have one.
[06:03] Lara Mendoza: A couple of nonfunctional asks: MFA enforced for all Redwood console users, IP allowlist for admin APIs, and quarterly penetration test reports. do you have pen-test history?
[06:13] Diego Alvarez: Redwood undergoes annual pentests and we have summaries we can share. MFA and IP allowlist are standard — MFA is required for admin. quarterly pen tests would be an extra cadence but we can discuss.
[06:24] Priya Rao: Ok. timeline recap?
[06:26] Maya Chen: Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) — exchange docs and network info; week 1-2 — spin up Dedicated pilot infra + SAML/console; week 3 — run baseline benchmarks; week 4 — analyze and tune; week 5 — quantized run; week 6 — final report and handoff. does that align?
[06:44] Evan Kim: Yes that looks fine. Just need the security package early so we can loop legal.
[06:49] Maya Chen: We'll get SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary, DPA, KMS guide, and sample audit event schema to you by 2025-07-23.
[06:58] Lara Mendoza: Please include the exact audit event keys — we need to map them into our SIEM parsers.
[07:03] Diego Alvarez: Will do; we'll include event name mapping and examples. note: some event names differ across internal versions, we'll give you the stable schema for the pilot.
[07:14] Priya Rao: Any blockers for scheduling the benchmark week of 7/28?
[07:17] Maya Chen: None on our side — Diego will coordinate runner images and credentials.
[07:21] Diego Alvarez: We'll need an infra point-of-contact from your side for VPC peering and security group work.
[07:27] Evan Kim: That's me. I'll coordinate with networking.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Great. last part — can we capture success criteria explicitly so we can sign-off at the end?
[07:34] Priya Rao: Sure: 1) p95 under 250ms on typical 600-token prompts, 2) token cost <= $0.0009 on 2k avg after quantization, 3) audit log export to eu-west-1 S3 and no PII in exported logs, 4) SAML SSO working with role mappings, 5) automated fallback functions.
[07:52] Diego Alvarez: We'll translate those into test cases in the benchmark harness.
[07:56] Maya Chen: Perfect. wrapping up — I'll send the security package and benchmark repo links, Diego will send runner images and sizing recommendation, Evan will provide prompts and traffic profile.
[08:06] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:09] Lara Mendoza: Thanks.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Thanks team, we'll follow up with calendar invites for kickoff and the benchmark window.

Meeting end notes:
- Slight transcription artifacts present (product names like 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicatd', 'KV cache' as 'K-V cash').
- Crossover talk at 00:36-00:42, minor dropouts during 05:00-05:10.
- Expected artifacts to be shared: security package (SOC2/ISO), DPA, KMS/BYOK guide, benchmark harness repo, network requirements doc.
